'''''Scilla bifolia''''', the '''alpine squill'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> or '''two-leaf squill''', is a [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] growing from an underground [[bulb]],<ref name=pign>Pignatti S. - Flora d'Italia - Edagricole – 1982 Vol. III, pg. 365</ref> belonging to the genus ''[[Scilla]]'' of the family [[Asparagaceae]].

The Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''bifolia'' means "twin leaved".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>

==Description==
''Scilla bifolia'' grows from a bulb {{convert|1|-|2|cm|1|abbr=on}} across.<ref name=pign/> There are two or rarely three lance-shaped, curved, fleshy and shiny leaves<ref name=pign/> and the bases of the leaves clasp up to about the half of the stem ([[wikt:amplexicaul|amplexicaul]]).<ref name=pign/>

The [[pedicel (botany)|flowering stems]] are erect and unbranched, {{convert|10|-|20|cm|0|abbr=on}} high.<ref name=pign/> The [[raceme]] bears 6-10 flowers, each {{convert|1|cm|1|abbr=on}} across.<ref name=pign/>

The flowers of ''Scilla bifolia'' are upward-facing, unlike the nodding flowers of ''[[Scilla siberica]]'' (Siberian squill). They bloom from early to late spring. The six [[tepal]]s are deep violet-blue, more rarely white, pink, or purple.<ref name=pign/> The fruit is a [[capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{convert|6|-|8|mm|1|abbr=on}} across.<ref name=pign/>

''S. bifolia'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHSPF>{{cite web | title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Scilla bifolia'' | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16835/Scilla-bifolia/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 9 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 6 November 2018}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''Scilla bifolia'' is native to [[Europe]] and western [[Russia]] south through [[Turkey]] to [[Syria]].<ref name=ars>{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}}</ref> The plant is found in shady places, woods of beech or deciduous trees, and mountain grasslands.<ref name=pign/> It grows at an altitude of {{convert|100|-|2000|m|abbr=on}} above sea level.<ref name=pign/>
